Czech

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Italian saldo.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈsaldo]

Noun

[edit]

saldo n

  1. balance (the difference between credit and debit of an account)
    Synonym: zůstatek

Declension

[edit]
Declension of saldo (hard neuter)
singular plural
nominative saldo salda
genitive salda sald
dative saldu saldům
accusative saldo salda
vocative saldo salda
locative saldu saldech
instrumental saldem saldy

[edit]

  • “saldo”, in Slovník spisovného jazyka českého (in Czech), 1960–1971, 1989
  • “saldo”, in Internetová jazyková příručka (in Czech), 2008–2026

Dutch

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Italian saldo.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈsɑl.doː/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Hyphenation: sal‧do

Noun

[edit]

saldo n (plural saldi or saldo's, diminutive saldootje n)

  1. balance on an account [from 16th c.]

Derived terms

[edit]
  • banksaldo
  • doelsaldo
  • salderen

Descendants

[edit]

  • → Indonesian: saldo
  • → West Frisian: saldo

Esperanto

[edit]
Esperanto Wikipedia has an article on:
saldo
Wikipedia eo

Etymology

[edit]

From Russian са́льдо (sálʹdo) and Polish saldo, both borrowed from Italian saldo. Compare French solde, Czech saldo, Spanish saldo, Swedish saldo.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈsaldo/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -aldo
  • Syllabification: sal‧do

Noun

[edit]

saldo (accusative singular saldon, plural saldoj, accusative plural saldojn)

  1. (accounting) balance (difference between credit and debit of an account)
    saldo debeta, kredita; favora saldo.

Derived terms

[edit]
  • saldado
  • saldi

See also

[edit]
  • bilanco (“balance sheet”)

Further reading

[edit]
  • “saldo”, in Plena Ilustrita Vortaro de Esperanto [Complete Illustrated Dictionary of Esperanto], 2020, →ISBN
  • “saldo”, in Reta Vortaro [Online Dictionary] (in Esperanto), 1997-2026

Etymology

[edit]

International banking term of Italian origin

Noun

[edit]

saldo (genitive [please provide], partitive [please provide])

  1. balance of an account

Finnish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Italian saldo.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈsɑldo/, [ˈs̠ɑ̝ldo̞]
  • Rhymes: -ɑldo
  • Syllabification(key): sal‧do
  • Hyphenation(key): sal‧do

Noun

[edit]

saldo

  1. balance (of an account)
    Synonym: varat pl
  2. (accounting) net balance (difference between the total of the debits and the total of the credits)
  3. (figuratively) result, score (in-some-way numeric result of an endeavor)

Indonesian

[edit]
Indonesian Wikipedia has an article on:
saldo
Wikipedia id

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Dutch saldo, from Italian saldo.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Indonesian) IPA(key): /ˈsaldo/ [ˈsal.do]
  • Rhymes: -aldo
  • Syllabification: sal‧do

Noun

[edit]

saldo (plural saldo-saldo)

  1. (accounting) balance: the difference between credit and debit of an account
    Synonym: baki (Malay)
  2. (business, finance) outstanding (stock held by shareholders)

Hyponyms

[edit]
  • saldo ATM
  • saldo awal
  • saldo bank
  • saldo debit
  • saldo imbangan
  • saldo kompensasi
  • saldo kredit
  • saldo laba
  • saldo minimal
  • saldo minimum
  • saldo piutang
  • saldo piutang pembiayaan
  • saldo pokok
  • saldo rekening
  • saldo terutang

Further reading

[edit]
  • “saldo”, in Kamus Besar Bahasa Indonesia [Great Dictionary of the Indonesian Language] (in Indonesian), Jakarta: Agency for Language Development and Cultivation – Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology of the Republic of Indonesia, 2016

Italian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈsal.do/
  • Rhymes: -aldo
  • Hyphenation: sàl‧do

Etymology 1

[edit]

Probably from a Vulgar Latin derivative of a crossing of Latin solidus with validus.[1] Doublet of soldo, solido, and sodo.

Adjective

[edit]

saldo (feminine salda, masculine plural saldi, feminine plural salde, superlative saldissimo, adverb saldamente)

  1. firm, steady
  2. sound
Related terms
[edit]
  • saldare

Etymology 2

[edit]

    Deverbal from saldare +‎ -o.

    Noun

    [edit]

    saldo m (plural saldi)

    1. settlement, payment
    2. balance
    3. sale (bargain event)
    Descendants
    [edit]
    • → Czech: saldo
    • → Dutch: saldo
      • Afrikaans: saldo
      • → Indonesian: saldo
      • → West Frisian: saldo
    • → Esperanto: saldo
    • → Estonian: saldo
    • → Finnish: saldo
    • → German: Saldo
    • → Macedonian: са́лдо (sáldo)
    • → Norwegian Bokmål: saldo
    • → Norwegian Nynorsk: saldo
    • → Polish: saldo
    • → Portuguese: saldo
    • → Russian: са́льдо (sálʹdo)
    • → Serbo-Croatian:
      • Latin script: sȃldo
      • Cyrillic script: са̑лдо
    • → Spanish: saldo
    • → Swedish: saldo

    Etymology 3

    [edit]

    See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

    Verb

    [edit]

    saldo

    1. first-person singular present indicative of saldare
